findings.issue: bb100Value takes the LCM of every bigBet in a 500-hand group. parseHandRecord only checks that stake.bigBet is a safe integer >= 1 and puts no limit on how many distinct values appear. Many distinct or coprime big bets push the LCM past 2^53, which makes it imprecise and gives a wrong BB/100. Eventually it overflows to Infinity. Then Infinity % b is NaN, and gcd(NaN, NaN) recurses until a 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' RangeError. statisticsView runs inside App.tsx's onFulfilled handler (line 90), so the second .then callback does not catch that throw. The result is an unhandled rejection, and the Statistics screen stays aria-busy forever instead of showing LOAD_FAILED_MESSAGE.
findings.evidence: A tampered IndexedDB hand record has cash stake.bigBet values that differ, for example about 30 coprime values near MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, or a few hundred distinct small ones. parseHandRecord accepts them. trendHand puts each in cash.bigBet. statisticsView calls bb100Points, then bb100Value, whose LCM reduce reaches Infinity. gcd then recurses without end and throws a RangeError, which escapes the onFulfilled handler. I confirmed this in node with 30 values near 2^53. Only someone who can already write this origin's IndexedDB can reach it, and it only denies them their own Statistics screen. Real play only stores the fixed table stakes, so the LCM stays small. No division by zero is possible because bigBet >= 1. Nothing is injected: all text is React-escaped and SVG attributes are numbers.
findings.fix: Optional defence in depth: compute Σ(net/bigBet) in floating point when the LCM is not a safe integer, or return early in gcd for non-finite inputs. Also move statisticsView(data) into the guarded path (for example, map it in an earlier .then) so a throw falls back to view: null (LOAD_FAILED_MESSAGE).

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. bigBet is validated as a safe integer >= 1, so there is no division by zero, and normal play produces only finite values. Net amounts are validated whole numbers, and the labels are numbers formatted with toFixed and rendered through React, so text cannot be injected. There are no new dependencies, no network use and no secrets. One MINOR: a tampered local store with many distinct big bets overflows the LCM. That leads to infinite gcd recursion, and the RangeError is not caught by the App's error branch, so the screen hangs on loading. The only effect is a self-inflicted denial of service.
